Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  April 24, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:10 p.m., on Monday, April 24, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  PÉREZ

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Public Works & Utilities Ray, Director of
Finance Lieu, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of
Community Development Ho, Director of Human Resources Ko, Chief of Police Kennedy

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Andrade-Stadler

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  COMMENDATIONS: OUTGOING COMMISSION MEMBERS – F2M23-3, F2M23-34

  The City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, recognized the City’s outgoing Board
  and Commission members for their outstanding and dedicated service to the City of Alhambra.
  Mayor Andrade-Stadler presented the Certificates of Service.

  GLENN BARNETT
  Parks & Recreation Commission
  (8 years)

  FRANK BODEMAN
  Parks & Recreation Commission
  (8 years)

  ANDREA GUTIERREZ
  Youth Commission
  (4 years)

  MEGHAN WEBSTER
  Youth Commission
  (4 years)

4-24-23
 2.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: PARKS CREW CHIEF GERARDO MOTA – F2M23-3

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and the City Council commended and thanked Parks Crew Chief
  Gerardo Mota for his 25 years of faithful and loyal service to the Parks & Recreation
  Department and the City of Alhambra. Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER presented a Certificate of
  Service plaque to Mr. Mota for his outstanding work for the City.

3.  PROCLAMATION: ARBOR DAY – F2M23-3

  The Alhambra City Council ratified the action of Mayor Andrade-Stadler in proclaiming April
  28, 2023 as ARBOR DAY in Alhambra. Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER presented the Arbor Day
  proclamation to Director of Parks & Recreation Michael Macias.

PRESENTATION

4.  STATE OF THE CITY ADDRESS – F2M23-16

  Mayor Andrade-Stadler provided insight on the current state of the City and the progress that
  has been made over the past year.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

5.  APPROPRIATE FUNDS TO EXECUTE THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE ALHAMBRA
  COMMUNITY CENTER THROUGH A SPECIFIED GRANT FUNDED BY THE CALIFORNIA
  BUDGET ACT OF 2022 AND ADMINISTERED THROUGH CALIFORNIA STATE PARKS –
  F2M18-54, F2M22-65, M2M23-62

  Director of Parks & Recreation MACIAS delivered a staff report. On March 27, 2023,
  Resolution No. R2M23-15 was approved and passed by the City Council authorizing the
  application and receipt of grant funds for the construction of a new community center pursuant
  to policies and procedures for local assistance specified grants. On April 17, 2023, staff
  received the grant contract for the project and the City Manager signed the agreement as
  designated by Resolution No. R2M23-15. In order to proceed with the development of this
  important community project, staff requested the City Council appropriate grant revenue and
  expenditure funds in the 2022-2023 Fiscal Year Budget. In addition, as with other community
  projects of this magnitude and complexity, staff recommended one and/or two
  Councilmembers provide support to the City’s consultant selection and project monitoring
  process. In this regard, Council involvement would provide valuable opportunity to successfully
  guide the project toward completion and in alignment with the Council’s expectations and
  provide opportunity to report regular updates to the entire Council.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MAZA expressed his enthusiasm for the project, discussed the
  timeline of the project, and noted that he would like to be part of the sub-committee.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER noted that she would like to be on the sub-committee as well.

  Action Taken:  City Council appropriated revenue and expenditure funds for the
  Specified Grant from the Budget Act of 2022, AB179, Chapter 249, Control Section 19.56,
  Item 3790-101-0001(k) Other Community Services, in the amount of $25,000,000; appointed
  Vice Mayor Maza and Mayor Andrade-Stadler to a Sub-Committee; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-62)
  2
4-24-23
   Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6-26)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item Nos. 8 and 23, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

6.  CONSIDERATION OF A CHIEF OF POLICE CONTRACT WITH GARRETT KENNEDY –
  F2M-71, F2M23-2, C2M23-20, M2M23-66

  Director of Human Resources KO delivered a staff report. Chief of Police Kelley Fraser recently
  notified the City Manager of plans to retire as of May 10, 2023. Garrett Kennedy was hired by
  the City on March 26, 2001 and during his tenure with the Alhambra Police Department, has
  risen through the ranks as Police Officer, Police Corporal, Police Sergeant, Police
  Lieutenant/Commander and most recently served as Assistant Chief of Police. Under the
  terms of the Employment Agreement, the Chief shall oversee the Police Department and its
  divisions; serve under the direction of the City Manager; and enforce the execution of all laws
  and ordinances governing the City of Alhambra.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MAZA welcomed incoming Chief of Police Kennedy and thanked
  outgoing Police Chief Fraser for her service to the City.

  Councilmember LEE thanked incoming Chief of Police Kennedy for his service to the City and
  expressed support for his appointment to Chief of Police.

  Councilmember MALONEY thanked both incoming Chief of Police Kennedy and outgoing
  Police Chief Fraser for their service to the City.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER wished outgoing Police Chief Fraser a happy retirement and
  congratulated incoming Chief of Police Kennedy.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved that certain Employment Agreement
  designating Garrett Kennedy as the Chief of Police effective May 11, 2023 on file in the Office
  of the City Clerk as Contract No. C2M23-20 and by this reference incorporated herein and
  made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein; authorized the City Manager to execute
  the Employment Agreement; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M23-66)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

7.  APPROVAL OF CONTRACT FOR FISCAL YEARS 2023-2024 AND 2024-2025 WITH THE
  ALHAMBRA CHAMBER OF COMMERCE – F2M21-43, C2M23-24, M2M23-55

  The City has contracted with the Chamber of Commerce for many years to provide promotional
  services on behalf of the City. Staff considered the services proposed for Fiscal Years 2023-
  25 and 2024-25 were essential to supporting the business community, engaging residents,
  promoting Alhambra, and encouraging partnerships within the community. The following is a
  3
4-24-23
   summary of a few of the services the Chamber of Commerce would be providing under the
  new contract: Participate with the City to support business retention and economic
  development efforts including providing ombudsman assistance between prospective and
  existing businesses and City staff; and regularly coordinate with property owners, commercial
  brokers, and developers to help address vacancies; Serve as Alhambra’s central information
  office for the community to promote Alhambra as a destination for businesses, residents,
  tourists, and Chamber members and non-members; Provide special events including Lunar
  New Year Celebration, Alhambra State of the City, and Rose Court Luncheon; Develop guides,
  informational brochures, and digital assets including Alhambra Eats, a marketing website for
  dining destinations for the community; and, Work with local schools to introduce students to
  local businesses and career opportunities including internships. Costs for the Chamber’s
  services were proposed in the FY 2023-25 budget. The cost of $240,000 (or $120,000 per
  fiscal year) represented no increase in contract costs from the current fiscal year.

  Public Comments via Email:

  The following individuals expressed concern with the City providing additional funds
  to the Chamber of Commerce:
  1) Melissa MICHELSON
  2) David ROCHA

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council executed a contract, subject of final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce in an amount not
  to exceed $120,000 for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 and $120,000 for Fiscal year 2024-2025; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-55)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

8.  BUDGET APPROPRIATION FOR THE CHAPEL AVENUE AFFORDABLE HOUSING
  PROJECT – F2M20-71, M2M23-56

  On January 31, 2022, the City entered into a Disposition and Development Agreement (“DDA”)
  for the construction of an affordable housing project on a surface parking lot adjacent to the
  City-owned parking structure on Chapel Avenue. The project proposed to build 44 affordable
  housing units on site. On February 27, 2023, the City Council authorized the City Manager to
  execute an amended and restated DDA with Chapel Housing Partners, L.P., as well as,
  various project implementing documents. On March 9, 2023, the City Manager executed an
  amended and restated DDA and various documents. As the closing date approaches, Chapel
  Housing Partners, L.P. would be required to draw funds from the Housing Asset Fund Account.
  Staff requested an appropriation of $4,500,000.00 from the Housing Asset Fund. There was
  sufficient funding from the Housing Asset Fund balance to cover the cost.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON, via Zoom, expressed his enthusiasm to see this
  project moving forward and inquired about the funding in the housing asset fund.

  City Manager BINNQUIST provided clarification.

  Discussion:  None

  4
4-24-23
   Action Taken:  City Council approved a budget appropriation for the Chapel affordable
  housing project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M23-56)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE 10-YARD DUMP TRUCK – F2M23-6A,
  C2M23-25, M2M23-57

  The current Public Works dump truck has been in service for 33 years and reached its
  expected life span for usage. As such, staff sought to purchase one dump truck to replace the
  aging vehicle though a cooperative purchase agreement. Cooperative purchase is allowable
  per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On August 5, 2021, Sourcewell opened four
  bids for the procurement of roadway maintenance equipment with related accessories,
  attachments, materials and supplies. Sourcewell awarded contract 080521-PBL to PB Loader
  on November 5, 2021 - a contract that would not expire until October 11, 2025. Sourcewell bid
  specifications included an option for purchasing dump trucks for road maintenance; therefore,
  staff recommended purchasing one new dump truck vehicle utilizing this option.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to PB Loader in an amount not to exceed $287,551.85 for
  the purchase of one 10-yard dump truck for the Public Works Department; and, directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-57)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: MAIN STREET SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT
  BETWEEN GRANADA AVENUE AND EL MOLINO STREET – F2M23-26, N2M23-24,
  C2M23-26, M2M23-57

  On February 27, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the Main Street Sewer Main Replacement Between Granada Avenue and El Molino Street.
  On March 30, 2023, bids were opened by the City Clerk. Ten bids were received, which ranged
  from base bid amounts of $673,020 to $1,622,700. GRBCON Inc. submitted the lowest
  qualified bid at $673,020.00. In addition to base bid amount, GRBCON Inc. submitted
  $37,859.00 under the Alternative Bid Schedule. Staff reviewed the bid submitted by GRBCON
  Inc. and found it to be in full compliance and conformance with the project specifications.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and GRBCON Inc.,
  for the Main Street Sewer Replacement Project between Granada Avenue and El Molino
  Street in an amount not to exceed $710,879.00; find the Main Street Sewer Replacement
  Project between Granada Avenue and El Molino Street categorically exempt from California
  5
4-24-23
   Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (b); and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-58)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR THE SEWER
  SYSTEM FLOW MONITORING AND CAPACITY ANALYSIS STUDY – F2M23-27,
  RFP2M23-4, C2M23-27

  On February 27, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for Engineering Design Services for the Sewer System Flow Monitoring and Capacity Analysis
  Study. Staff reviewed and evaluated the proposal received. Based on qualifications,
  experience, reputation, responsiveness, availability and cost, Utility systems, Science &
  Software, Inc. was selected as the most responsive firm.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and Utility Systems,
  Science & Software, Inc. for the Sewer System Flow Monitoring and Capacity Analysis Study
  in an amount not to exceed $83,665.00; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-59)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

12.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: FRONT STREET WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT AND ZONE
  CHANGE - PHASE 1 – F2M19-20, N2M23-45

  Currently, Mission Road is the dividing line between the South Zone and North Zone - the two
  major pressure zones in the City. The break in pressure zones existed because of the
  topography of the City. With the pressure zone break at its current location, residents along
  Front Street experienced low water pressure. Hydraulic testing conducted in the area of Front
  Street between Marengo and Atlantic showed that moving the zone break south to Shorb
  Street and replacing the existing four-inch cast iron water mains in this area would significantly
  increase the water pressure and fire flow capability in the area. The project involved
  construction in three phases, sequentially over the next three years with one section of the
  project occurring each year. This project was Phase 1 which would be on Front Street from
  Atlantic Boulevard to Olive Avenue.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change - Phase
  1 with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on May 25, 2023 and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same
  day.

  6
4-24-23
   Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

13.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: REHABLITATION OF THE STORM DRAIN ON MONTEZUMA
  AVENUE – F2M23-40, N2M23-46

  The City of Alhambra Utilities Department is responsible for inspection, maintenance and
  repair of the storm drain system in the public right-of-way and in drainage easements. The
  storm drain pipe at Montezuma Avenue, located from 2801 Montezuma Avenue to Ramona
  Avenue, was broken and needed to be repaired to handle normal water flow before flooding
  occurs. Due to the pipe passing through many private properties, the pipe lining method is a
  preferable way to repair the pipe. This storm drain pipe was 36-inch in diameter and
  approximately 350 feet in length. Plans and specifications were prepared; staff reviewed the
  plans and found them to be consistent with City standards.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain on Montezuma Avenue Project
  with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on May 18, 2023, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same
  day.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

14.  RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE ALL DOCUMENTS
  AND AGREEMENTS FOR PROJECTS FUNDED THROUGH THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION (CALTRANS) ON BEHALF OF THE CITY –
  F2M23-18, R2M23-25

  The City of Alhambra was eligible to receive state and federal funding for various transportation
  projects through the State of California Department of Transportation (Caltrans). To ensure
  receipt of state and federal funding for these projects, the City Council must adopt a resolution
  designating the City Manager as the authorized official to execute documents and agreements
  for projects funded through Caltrans. Additionally, from time to time, the City submits grant
  applications for state or federally funded programs. The City was awarded state or federally
  funded grants for Capital Improvements Projects, which were managed by the Public Works
  Department. The state or federally funded grants, administered by Caltrans, required
  submittals from the City at the time of submission of the grant application, at the acceptance
  of the grant, during the grant project implementation, and/or following the grant project
  completion. In order to comply with the state and federal requirements on certain submittals,
  staff recommended having the City Manager or her designee sign all state and federally funded
  documents.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-25 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute all

  7
4-24-23
   documents and agreements for projects funded through the State of California Department of
  Transportation (Caltrans)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

15.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A REVISED SIDE LETTER OF AGREEMENT AMENDING THE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF AHAMBRA AND THE
  ALHAMBRA POLICE DISPATCH ASSOCIATION – F2M23-2, C2M21-51, R2M23-22

  Following the City Council’s approval of the Side Letter with the Alhambra Police Dispatch
  Association (APDA) at the Council meeting of April 10, 2023, staff discovered a clerical error
  that incorrectly referenced the wrong fiscal years and effective dates for the salary increases
  that were agreed upon. The revised side letter reflects the corrected fiscal years and effective
  dates for the salary increases. Adoption of a resolution to implement these revised changes
  and to correct the record was required.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-22 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving a Revised Side Letter amending the Memorandum of
  Understanding between the City of Alhambra and the Alhambra Police Dispatch Association
  and amending the City of Alhambra Compensation Plan, superseding Resolution No. R2M23-
  18

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

16.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A THIRD SIDE LETTER OF AGREEMENT WITH THE
  ALHAMBRA MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES’ ASSOCIATION FOR A POSITION TITLE
  CHANGE – F2M23-2, C2M17-70, R2M23-24

  Following the resignation of an employee in November 2022, City staff conducted two
  recruitments, each time attempting to fill a vacancy in the Marketing and Community
  Engagement Specialist position. Both recruitments failed to produce viable and qualified
  candidates to fill the position. Following the failed recruitments, staff researched comparable
  positions within the field and discovered similar positions to possess “Public Information”
  and/or “Communications” within their titles. Therefore, in order to bring the position title in line
  with industry standards, a title change from Marketing and Community Engagement Specialist
  to Public Information Specialist was proposed to the Alhambra Management Employees’
  Association (AMEA). The City and AMEA have conferred and reached agreement regarding
  amending the existing MOU and class specification from Marketing and Community
  Engagement Specialist to Public Information Specialist. Adoption of a resolution approving
  the third Side Letter Agreement is necessary to memorialize the change.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-24 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving a Third Side Letter to the Memorandum of
  8
4-24-23
   Understanding between the City of Alhambra and the Alhambra Management Employees’
  Association to memorialize AMEA’s agreement to change the title of the classification of
  Marketing and Community Engagement Specialist to Public Information Specialist in the
  existing Memorandum of Understanding and to the class specification.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

17.  RESOLUTION DECLARING CITY’S INTENTION TO DISPOSE OF REAL PROPERTY AND
  SETTING THE DATE FOR A PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER THE DISPOSITION OF
  PROPERTY ADJACENT TO STORY PARK – F2M21-22, R2M23-23

  In January 2021, the City received a complaint from a neighbor regarding leaves falling from
  an oak tree from a vacant, adjacent property creating a hazard on Story Place. Staff
  investigated the matter and determined the property in question was part of Story Park. The
  investigation also revealed the land was landlocked and only accessible through the six
  adjacent residential properties. Given the location and status of this landlocked, unimproved
  and publicly inaccessible property, staff believed the property was more properly reconfigured
  to be part of the adjacent residential properties. This would eliminate maintenance and liability
  issues for the City. In April 2022, the City Council directed staff to move forward to dispose of
  the property. Pursuant to California Government Code §38503, before the disposition of such
  property, the City Council was required to adopt a Resolution of Intention describing the
  proposed abandonment of property and to fix a time, at least thirty days after adoption of the
  Resolution of Intention, when it would consider and take action to order all or any portion of
  the park abandoned and the land sold or otherwise transferred. This public hearing was
  scheduled for June 26, 2023. The Lot Line Adjustment, General Plan Amendment, and Zone
  Change applications, along with a Resolution declaring the Property to be exempt surplus
  under provisions of California Government Code §54220, et seq. (the “Surplus Land Act”),
  would also be presented to the City Council on that date.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-23 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, declaring its intention to dispose of real
  property and setting the date for a meeting to consider the disposition of property declaring
  the City’s intention to dispose of the unimproved real property approximately 12,937 square
  feet in size that is part of Story Park (APN 5337-002-900) but is separated from the improved
  portion of Story Park by a concrete channel known as the San Pascual Wash, and set a Public
  Hearing date of June 26, 2023 at 6:00 p.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be heard,
  to consider and take action to order that landlocked, inaccessible and unimproved portion of
  the park abandoned and the land transferred.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

18.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH CALTRANS
  FOR THE 710 STUB IMPROVEMENTS INTO A FOUR-LANE ARTERIAL AND
  APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS – F2M19-32, C2M23-28, M2M23-60

  9
4-24-23
   On March 13, 2023, the City Council authorized a Cooperative Agreement with Caltrans for
  the Fremont Ramp and Interchange Improvements as part of the “Advancing Alhambra”
  project to improve local roads and safety for residents and reduce traffic and congestion in
  Alhambra. Alhambra’s traffic studies in 2020 and scoping in 2021 identified specific locations
  for mobility improvement consideration including the on/off ramps at Fremont, Atlantic, Garfield
  and the conversion of the 710 Stub at Valley into a four-lane arterial. The improvements were
  anticipated to keep motorists on the I-10 rather than encourage repeat cut through via
  Alhambra’s streets and neighborhoods. Since traffic would be more efficient with less
  congestion, the improvements would aid in reducing idling and improving air quality in
  Alhambra. This Cooperative Agreement was specifically for those improvements along the 710
  Stub at Valley. The project would reduce the Stub from a six-lane freeway corridor to a four-
  lane local arterial. Featured with the new arterial are biking lanes, a pedestrian walkway,
  lighting, parkways with trees and landscape, and stormwater pre-treatment elements including
  water capture and reuse elements.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized entering into a Cooperative Agreement,
  subject to review and approval by the City Manager and the City Attorney, by and between the
  City of Alhambra and the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) for the Project
  Initiation Document (PID) for the 710 Stub Improvements Into a Four-Lane Arterial; approved
  an appropriation of funds in the amount of $200,000 for Caltrans’ review of the project; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s actions. (M2M23-60)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  PÉREZ

19.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ALMANSOR COURT EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT –
  F2M23-41, N2M23-47

  On January 23, 2023, the City Council approved the reallocation of American Rescue Plan
  Act (ARPA) funds not to exceed $481,942 to fund certain Almansor Court Exterior
  Improvement Projects. Specifications and bid documentation were completed for the
  Almansor Court Exterior Improvement Project. The project would include new paint and stucco
  to the exterior of the Almansor Court building. Bids would be due no later than 10:30 a.m. on
  May 25, 2023, in the office of the City Clerk and would be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same
  day.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to

   Staff recommended the purchase of a Direct Recirculating Apparatus Firefighting Training &
  Sustainability (DRAFTS) unit from PumpPod USA. The mobile DRAFTS unit employed
  recycled water versus tapping hydrant water for each evolution. The system utilized a catch
  trailer for a firefighter or an apparatus to direct water flow into a recycling chamber. The water
  was recycled, reused, and stored after each training. The unit with the portable hydrant allowed
  the Department to train firefighters with full flowing water. In addition, the Engine Companies
  could train without having to call “Out of Service” thus significantly increasing the hours of
  training but reducing time and costs related to these exercises. The Fire Department was
  awarded a grant in the amount of $203,000.00 for Urban Search and Rescue (US & R)
  equipment, supplies, and training from the State Homeland Security Grant Program. The
  purchase of the unit would be covered by this grant. Pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code
  3.36.080 (B)(2), the purchase method may be dispensed when the equipment can only be
  obtained from one source (sole source).

23.  ADOPTION OF THE 2023 STRATEGIC PLAN – F2M23-35, M2M23-65

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly of Kelly
  Associates Management Group held a Special Council Meeting for a Strategic Planning
  Session on March 30, 2023 to update the City’s current Strategic Plan (adopted in 2021).
  Following the meeting, staff met to review the Council’s goals and objectives and discuss
  strategy and status of the new and updated strategic plan ideas with detailed goals and metrics
  to guide staff. On April 17, 2023, the City Council held a second special Council meeting to
  review all of the items on the updated 2023 Strategic Plan. The new Strategic Plan contained
  six Goals, defined: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety; Goal 2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility;
  Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base (Economic Development);
  Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and,
  Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities. Staff would bring updates on the 2023 Strategic Plan
  to the Council on a quarterly basis.
